mn22:1.2: On one occasion the Blessed One was staying at Savatthi in Jeta’s Grove, Anathapindika’s park.
mn22:2.1: Now on that occasion this pernicious viewpoint (ditthigata) had arisen in the monk Arittha Formerly-of-the-Vulture-Killers:
mn22:2.2: “As I understand the Dhamma taught by the Blessed One, those acts the Blessed One says are obstructive, when indulged in, are not genuine obstructions.”
mn22:2.3: A large number of monks heard,
mn22:2.4: “They say that this pernicious viewpoint has arisen in the monk Arittha Formerly-of-the-Vulture-Killers:
mn22:2.5: ‘As I understand the Dhamma taught by the Blessed One, those acts the Blessed One says are obstructive, when indulged in, are not genuine obstructions.’”
mn22:3.1: So they went to the monk Arittha Formerly-of-the-Vulture-Killers and on arrival said to him,
mn22:3.2: “Is it true, friend Arittha, that this pernicious viewpoint has arisen in you —
mn22:3.3: ‘As I understand the Dhamma taught by the Blessed One, those acts the Blessed One says are obstructive, when indulged in, are not genuine obstructions’?”
mn22:3.4: “Yes, indeed, friends. I understand the Dhamma taught by the Blessed One, and those acts the Blessed One says are obstructive, when indulged in are not genuine obstructions.”
mn22:3.5: Then those monks, desiring to pry the monk Arittha Formerly-of-the-Vulture-Killers away from that pernicious viewpoint, quizzed him back and forth and rebuked him, saying,
mn22:3.6: “Don't say that, friend Arittha. Don't misrepresent the Blessed One, for it is not good to misrepresent the Blessed One. The Blessed One would not say anything like that.
mn22:3.7: In many ways, friend, the Blessed One has described obstructive acts, and when indulged in they are genuine obstructions.
mn22:3.8: The Blessed One has said that sensual pleasures are of little satisfaction, much stress, much despair, & greater drawbacks.
mn22:3.9: The Blessed One has compared sensual pleasures to a chain of bones: of much stress, much despair, & greater drawbacks.
mn22:3.10: The Blessed One has compared sensual pleasures to a lump of flesh…
mn22:3.16: a butcher’s ax and chopping block…
mn22:3.18: a snake’s head: of much stress, much despair, & greater drawbacks.”
mn22:3.19: And yet even though he was quizzed back & forth and rebuked by those monks, the monk Ariṭṭha Formerly-of-the-Vulture-Killers, through stubbornness and attachment to that very same evil viewpoint, continued to insist,
mn22:3.20: “Yes, indeed, friends. I understand the Dhamma taught by the Blessed One, and those acts the Blessed One says are obstructive, when indulged in are not genuine obstructions.”
mn22:3.21: So when the monks were unable to pry the monk Ariṭṭha Formerly-of-the-Vulture-Killers away from that evil viewpoint, they went to the Blessed One and on arrival, having bowed down to him, sat to one side. As they were sitting there, they [told him what had happened].
mn22:5.1: So the Blessed One told a certain monk,
mn22:5.2: “Come, monk. In my name, call the monk Ariṭṭha Formerly-of-the-Vulture-Killers, saying,
mn22:5.4: “As you say, lord,” the monk responded and, having gone to the monk Ariṭṭha Formerly-of-the-Vulture-Killers, on arrival he said,
mn22:5.6: “As you say, my friend,” the monk Ariṭṭha Formerly-of-the-Vulture-Killers responded. Then he went to the Blessed One and, on arrival, having bowed down to him, sat to one side. As he was sitting there, the Blessed One said to him,
mn22:5.7: “Is it true, Ariṭṭha, that this evil viewpoint has arisen in you—
mn22:5.8: ‘As I understand the Dhamma taught by the Blessed One, those acts the Blessed One says are obstructive, when indulged in, are not genuine obstructions’?”
mn22:5.9: “Yes, indeed, lord. I understand the Dhamma taught by the Blessed One, and those acts the Blessed One says are obstructive, when indulged in are not genuine obstructions.”
mn22:6.1: “Worthless man, from whom have you understood that Dhamma taught by me in such a way?
mn22:6.2: Worthless man, haven’t I in many ways described obstructive acts? And when indulged in they are genuine obstructions.
mn22:6.3: I have said that sensual pleasures are of little satisfaction, much stress, much despair, & greater drawbacks.
mn22:6.4: I have compared sensual pleasures to a chain of bones: of much stress, much despair, & greater drawbacks.
mn22:6.5: I have compared sensual pleasures to a lump of flesh…
mn22:6.11: a butcher’s ax and chopping block…
mn22:6.13: a snake’s head: of much stress, much despair, & greater drawbacks.
mn22:6.14: But you, worthless man, through your own wrong grasp (of the Dhamma), have both slandered us as well as injuring yourself and accumulating much demerit for yourself,
mn22:6.15: for that will lead to your long-term harm & suffering.”
mn22:7.1: Then the Blessed One said to the monks,
mn22:7.3: Is this monk Ariṭṭha Formerly-of-the-Vulture-Killers even warm in this Dhamma & Vinaya?”
mn22:7.6: When this was said, the monk Ariṭṭha Formerly-of-the-Vulture-Killers sat silent, abashed, his shoulders drooping, his head down, brooding, at a loss for words.
mn22:7.7: Then the Blessed One, seeing that the monk Ariṭṭha Formerly-of-the-Vulture-Killers was sitting silent, abashed, his shoulders drooping, his head down, brooding, at a loss for words, said to him,
mn22:7.8: “Worthless man, you will be recognized for your own evil viewpoint.
mn22:7.9: I will cross-examine the monks on this matter.”
mn22:8.1: Then the Blessed One addressed the monks,
mn22:8.2: “Monks, do you, too, understand the Dhamma as taught by me in the same way that the monk Ariṭṭha Formerly-of-the-Vulture-Killers does when, through his own wrong grasp, he both slanders us as well as injuring himself and accumulating much demerit for himself?”
